messages.body:
Hey Ray,

My name's Piper Reeves with Everlight Ventures. I came across your property on Englewood Street in Memphis and wanted to reach out personally rather than send something generic.

I know you're based in Georgia now, which tells me you've probably got this place tied up from a distance for a while. That can work fine, but it also means you're carrying costs month to month with no one on site to manage things.

I'm not calling to pressure you into anything. Mostly curious if you'd ever thought about selling it off, especially if the timing lined up right. We work with folks in your exact situation all the time   we buy as is, handle everything on our end, and close on your timeline. No agent commissions, no months of showings, no back and forth with buyers.

If you're open to a conversation, I'd love to chat for ten minutes and see if it makes sense. And if not, no hard feelings at all.

Open to talking?

Piper Reeves
Outreach, Everlight Ventures

Reply STOP to opt out of future messages.
Yeah I have thought about offloading it. It is an old rental and I am out in Georgia now. It needs work. What can you actually do on it?

Hi Ray -- Henry here, picking up from Piper.

Thanks for being open to talking through this. You've got an older rental that's been a drag, and I get why offloading it makes sense, especially from Georgia. Let me walk you through exactly what we do and how the math works.

We buy properties as is. That means no repairs on your dime, no cleanup, no months listing and waiting for the right buyer. You own a 1912 single family on Englewood that needs work. We handle all of it -- the rehab, any tenant issues, liens, title problems, the whole load. We close on your timeline, you get cash into your account, and you're done.

Here's the market snapshot on Memphis rentals like yours. Median price is sitting at 195K, days on market average 32, and holding costs on a property that isn't performing run about 343 a month. That tells me every month you carry it, you're losing ground.

Our offer is 15,120 for the property as is, cash close. That number reflects what we can put to work on a full rehab, what the market absorbs, and what gets you certainty and speed instead of uncertainty and time. No agent commissions, no buyer finance falling through, no back and forth.

This isn't pressure -- Piper was right to say that. But it's a real number, and I want to be straight with you on it so you can decide whether it makes sense.

What questions do you have on the offer or the process.

Henry Hammond
Acquisitions, Everlight Ventures

Reply STOP to opt out of future messages.

Hi Ray,

Thanks for your response. I appreciate you coming back with a number. Let me walk through the math so we're on the same page.

You're at 23,040. Here's what I'm seeing on the acquisition side.

The property is a 1912 single family on Englewood that needs work. Current appraisal sits at 38,400. When I layer in repair costs (you mentioned it needs work), holding time, and what the market is actually moving at right now in Memphis, the math points us to 16,500 as the strong play.

Here's why that number makes sense for you. We close fast, all cash, no agent commissions eating 5 to 6 percent, no months of showings, no inspections that kill deals. You're in Georgia, you don't have to manage this remotely or travel back. We handle everything, tenants included. That's certainty and speed you don't get on the open market.

I know that's a gap from where you landed. But I want to be straight with you, Ray. The repair scope and timeline to retail push the math to 16,500. That's where we can move.

Where do you want to go from here.

Henry Hammond
Acquisitions, Everlight Ventures
